signal: Matroid raised a $20M Series B to expand its computer vision platform into manufacturing, industrial IoT, and video security

email.body1:
Adam, saw Matroid raise its $20M Series B to push computer vision into manufacturing and industrial IoT.

Expanding into new verticals usually means more in-market accounts than an enterprise team can cover before they cool, and that is where deals go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Matroid off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Adam, quick follow-up for Matroid.

Post-raise, board expectations on pipeline usually climb faster than headcount can, and a new vertical adds coverage gaps. Most teams don't actually know how many meetings they need to hit the new number, so the gap shows up late.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Matroid needs across manufacturing and IoT accounts this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Adam, last bit of proof for Matroid.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Matroid's reply rate likely compares to other Series-B startups. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?
email.body4:
Adam, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling enterprise pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Timing is everything right after a raise, and a vertical expansion is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to an enterprise computer-vision motion? I'll tailor it to Matroid either way.
